correctness.rationale: Explicitly enumerate all edge allocation patterns. For two points on one long edge and one on its opposite, the exact third-coordinate acceptance interval w(r) is derived from three positive Euclidean dot products; its integral gives the displayed closed J(L). Primitive differentiation and asymptotic expansion yield leading coefficients 3 and -3/2. Every remaining pattern is rigorously bounded in total by (12(2+4 log L)+8+48/L)/(8(L+1)^3), which is O(log L/L^3). The finite symbolic and quadrature checks independently reproduce intermediate integral identities. Right-angle and collinear cases are handled by the precise strict-acuteness definition.

value.rationale: Acute-triangle probabilities depend essentially on whether random points are drawn from interiors or boundaries. The natural degeneration from square to arbitrarily thin rectangles exhibits an unexpected logarithmic singularity rather than a pure inverse-power rare-event law. The result isolates the unique dominant facet occupancy pattern, determines both sharp leading constants, and supplies a fully explicit finite-aspect remainder estimate. The result is not simply a fixed-shape table recomputation.
